lxc_e5d46141350f121f.text: Wedding meals have always done more than feed guests.

lxc_1e959562af978dc5.text: The food on the table signals who the family is, what they believe, and how much they want to celebrate.

lxc_d7adec742de173c8.text: Because patricians belonged to Rome's upper class, this simple grain food carried legal, religious, and social meaning.

lxc_a8ad670b4f98d835.text: Records of medieval French feasts help us understand how a noble wedding banquet could make status visible.

lxc_80e25ed007380509.text: Aristocratic tables might offer peacock, heron, or swan.

lxc_6c3dab75e10a1dd2.text: Imported spices such as saffron, ginger, nutmeg, cardamom, and cinnamon came from far-off places.

lxc_95dd323737c2054a.text: Even the seating could show rank: the most important guest sat nearest the large salt container.

lxc_60752d3d5204a73e.text: It changes by region, community, and family.
